newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks stronger at open, results focus.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks stronger at open, results focus.

text.p: The Australian share market firmed at the open on Wednesday with the leaders making light gains in a results-focussed market.
The All Ordinaries index climbed 9.4 points to 2,717.0.
Best among the leaders was global mining giant Rio Tinto which added 1.3 percent to A$20.75 (US$15.36) early after a firmer performance in London trading.
"Results are clearly what people are waiting for," said a dealer at a Sydney-based investment bank.
First off the rank this morning was contract mining engineer Henry Walker Ltd, which reported an 18.5 percent higher full year net profit of A$20.99 million. Its shares added nine cents to A$2.72.
Still sizzling after Tuesday's surge in full year profit was West Australian-based diversified group Wesfarmers Ltd whose shares jumped 40 cents to a record high of A$13.00.
"They are back to their highs. It was certainly a strong result," the dealer said.
Wesfarmer's full year net profit leapt to A$139.6 million from A$92.79 million in the previous corresponding period.
Wesfarmer's 51 percent shareholder The Franked Income Fund felt the flow on benefits, adding 10 cents to a record high A$4.10.
The remaining major result expected today is from soft drink bottler Coca-Cola Amatil, due late in the day. Its shares were 17 cents higher at A$16.25.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about seven to six, while about 42 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
